questions.why: Superman's own creators, Jerry Siegel (words) and Joe Shuster (art), also made his arch-nemesis.

questions.q: In which year did Lex Luthor first appear in Action Comics #23?
questions.why: Luthor debuted in Action Comics #23, dated April 1940.

questions.q: Which 1986 miniseries by Marv Wolfman and John Byrne remade Luthor as a corporate tycoon instead of a mad scientist?
questions.why: After Crisis, Wolfman and Byrne redesigned Luthor in The Man of Steel as a corrupt business executive.

questions.q: What is the name of Lex Luthor's corporation in the comics?
questions.why: Luthor's company dominates Metropolis; in some stories it grows into a world-spanning conglomerate.

questions.q: When he becomes U.S. President in the comics, to whom does Lex hand control of his company beforehand?
questions.why: Before taking office he passed leadership of his firm to Talia al Ghul; his presidency collapsed in the Public Enemies story.

questions.q: Who played Lex Luthor opposite Christopher Reeve in the Superman films?
questions.why: Gene Hackman played Luthor in the Superman film series that began in 1978.

questions.q: Which actor played Lex Luthor in the 2006 film Superman Returns?
questions.why: Kevin Spacey took the role in 2006's Superman Returns.

questions.q: Who voiced Lex Luthor in Superman: The Animated Series and Justice League Unlimited?
questions.why: Clancy Brown voiced Luthor from the 1996 Superman series through Justice League Unlimited.

questions.q: Which comic storyline sees Luthor join the Justice League after the Crime Syndicate threat?
questions.why: After Forever Evil, Luthor joined the League, with the team reasoning that keeping him close made him easier to watch.

questions.q: Which studio artist is blamed for the mistake that left Lex Luthor bald?
questions.why: A slip by Leo Nowak, who worked on the Superman newspaper strip, swapped Luthor's red hair for a bald head.
